findings.summary: Sign-Off M2 fails: Does intro carry where, firstThing and readAloud? (intro missing: readAloud)
findings.actual: A scene with no authored first thing starts with the GM thinking.

findings.summary: Sign-Off M5 fails: Does the scene either have a speaking cast with wants, opensWith, a voice register and a sample line each, or say in its notes that it deliberately has no cast? (no cast at all, and nothing in notes says that is deliberate -- a forgotten cast looks identical to this)
findings.actual: A cast member without a want is scenery with a name. Walk-ons are exempt via walkOn: true. The first version tested only 'no INCOMPLETE cast members', which an empty cast satisfies trivially -- The Road In passed it correctly, and a scene that simply forgot its cast would have passed identically.

findings.summary: Sign-Off M8 fails: Does the scene offer at least two genuinely different skills, or say in its notes why one route is the design? (no skilled check in this scene at all)
findings.actual: The corpus attractor problem: one skill sat on 66% of checks while every per-scene audit read clean. Intake Medicals' five single-skill rungs are the legitimate exception and say so.

findings.summary: Sign-Off M10 fails: Does every beat delivered at the table have read-aloud or spoken text authored for it? (intro has no readAloud)
findings.actual: A table-delivery beat with only direction is a stage note where a line should be.

findings.summary: Sign-Off M11 fails: Does the scene say what to write down -- carryForward, outro.writeDown, or both? (nothing says what to write down when this closes)
findings.actual: What is not recorded when a scene closes is what next session's writing cannot use.

findings.summary: Sign-Off M13 fails: Is there at least one temptation -- a line ready to say when nobody is biting? (nothing to say to a table that is not biting)
findings.actual: A scene needs something to offer a quiet table that is not the GM asking 'so what do you do?'

findings.summary: Sign-Off S1 fails: Does the scene declare a real coordinate at each edge -- where the party is when it opens and where they are when it closes? (opens with no locationRef and is not `scattered` -- every other state owes a real coordinate)
findings.actual: Ingram, 2026-09-22, correcting a miscommunication: "I don't want to just track if the group splits or merges, I want to literally have a set of coordinates for the players to move between." The coordinate is the point. `intro.position.locationRef` and `outro.position.locationRef` are what the Scene Runner's automatic cut to the world map runs on -- core/travel-trigger.mjs's needsTravel fires on a locationRef CHANGE and does nothing at all when either side is null. `scattered` is the one legitimate no-coordinate edge, reserved for the campaign's own opening.

findings.summary: Sign-Off S7 fails: Does this scene's close leave every PC somewhere the NEXT scene can legitimately open from? (closes with no coordinate, and not `scattered`)
findings.actual: The forward half of the same question. A scene that ends well for itself and badly for its successor is only visible from here, because neither scene's own review can see it.

findings.summary: Sign-Off S11 fails: Does the automatic cut to the world map actually fire on the way into this scene? (no coordinate to leave the-errand from -- the cut to the world map will NOT fire, and the table is simply somewhere else with no error raised)
findings.actual: The whole scene -> map -> scene loop is already built and wired (foundry/scene-runner.mjs calls needsTravel at three sites; foundry/travel.mjs plans a real route across the road graph and animates it). It degrades in the worst possible way: when either end has no locationRef the cut is skipped SILENTLY, with no error anywhere, and the table is simply somewhere else next beat. Measured 2026-09-22: 7 of 25 scene changes fire; 17 are silent hard cuts.
